clue.text: Tax official has to take a cutter to island

parts.note: to take a cutter to something is to cut it out, to excise it
the Isle of Man is the island in question

explanation.surface: A taxman sails off to an island with a cutter, a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' pretends to be a boat; here taking a cutter to something means cutting it out.
explanation.definitionFit: An exciseman was an officer who collected excise duties, so a historical tax collector.

clue.text: Without honour, editor is in fix

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the editor's letters surround the honour

parts.note: the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: An editor who has no decoration is in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside; 'fix' is a verb, to set firmly.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to set it firmly within a surrounding mass.

clue.text: Relative getting up to dance in church

indicators.note: in places the turned dance within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

indicators.note: getting up in a down clue means the dance is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the tango is a dance

explanation.surface: A family member gets up to dance in church.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'getting up' means read from the bottom upwards; the church is the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognate means related by descent, so a kinsman or a word of common origin.

clue.text: Female will support Ancient Mariner

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
'll is the shortened form of will
to back someone is to support them

explanation.surface: A woman promises to support Coleridge's old sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ancient Mariner' evokes Coleridge's poem but means simply a seasoned sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A shellback is slang for an old, experienced sailor, especially one who has crossed the equator.

clue.text: Traditional steps taken as main record's broken

indicators.note: broken says the letters of the record phrase are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Customary dance steps performed when a big record is broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record's' supplies its S as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Morris dancing is a traditional English folk dance with set patterns of footwork.

clue.text: Show no end of accord?

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of accord

explanation.surface: Someone shows endless agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole, the clue describes a gesture that shows agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head is a gesture showing assent or agreement.

clue.text: Composer's ignorance?

definitions.meaning: Sir Arthur ... was an English composer, Master of the Queen's Music
from the proverb that ignorance: the question mark marks this playful equation

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb equates not knowing with happiness, and Arthur Bliss was a twentieth-century English composer.

clue.text: He appears when don's out of town

indicators.note: out of says the don is removed from the town's name

parts.note: Basildon is a town in Essex, England

explanation.surface: Someone turns up whenever the university lecturer leaves town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' is the definition: a man's name. 'don's' is 'don is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is a man's first name, so it can stand for a male person.

clue.text: One serial broadcast from Mediterranean country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: broadcast, like seed scattered, means the letters of serial are scattered

explanation.surface: A TV serial is broadcast from somewhere around the Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges SERIAL into SRAELI.
explanation.definitionFit: An Israeli adjective describes someone or something belonging to Israel, on the eastern Mediterranean.

clue.text: Observer magazine

definitions.meaning: an observer is someone who watches

explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches an event, and The Spectator is a long-running British political weekly.

clue.text: It's a mistake to tolerate such a frightful thing

parts.note: a bug is a mistake or fault, as in software
to bear something is to tolerate or put up with it

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that putting up with something so dreadful is an error.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear was originally a goblin used to frighten children, hence any object of dread.

clue.text: Merit of French answer

parts.note: de is French for of
to answer a purpose is to serve it, as in 'that will serve'

explanation.surface: A question about the worth of a French reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something is to be worthy of it, to earn it by one's conduct.

clue.text: Drag lake, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: to drag something is to draw or haul it
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Police dragging a lake, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a manner of speaking' looks like a hedge on the surface; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow, lengthened way of pronouncing vowels is a recognisable style of talking.

clue.text: Rude about vessel's bow being on the rocks

indicators.note: about means the first word's synonym goes round the letter taken from the vessel

parts.note: rude and insolent both describe disrespectful behaviour

indicators.note: a ship's bow is its front, so the first letter of vessel is taken

explanation.surface: A coarse remark about a ship's bow as it runs aground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' seems to describe the vessel, but it is the definition, meaning bankrupt; V goes inside INSOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is failing financially, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: Business manager is reserve member of team

parts.note: a store is a reserve or stock
a keeper, such as a goalkeeper or wicketkeeper, is a member of a team

explanation.surface: A firm's manager is a substitute player in the team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserve member of team' looks like one sporting phrase; it splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: A storekeeper runs a shop or manages a stock of supplies.

clue.text: Subordinate in Near East

parts.note: by means near, as in 'stand by me'
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A junior official stationed in the Near East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near East' reads as a region; it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Bye as an adjective means secondary or incidental, as in a bye-law or by-election.

clue.text: Liberal in seat appears to fall from grace

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for Liberal within the seat

parts.note: one's seat is one's backside

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician in a parliamentary seat appears disgraced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seat' suggests Parliament; it is the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To backslide is to relapse into bad habits, lapsing from virtue.

clue.text: Hearing expert's making record with one in a studio, perhaps

indicators.note: in says the record and the numeral are placed within the rearranged studio letters
perhaps says the letters of a studio are only one possible arrangement, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A specialist in hearing makes a recording, with someone else in a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges A STUDIO into AUDIOST; 'in' puts LOG and I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Audiology is the science of hearing, and its practitioner tests and treats hearing loss.

clue.text: Where one came to terms with stale fish

parts.note: stale means old, not fresh
a school is a group of fish

explanation.surface: A place where someone reached agreement over some old fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came to terms' means attended school terms, not reached agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: One's former school is where one spent school terms, punning on reaching agreement.

clue.text: Lacking courage, paid only a little money

parts.note: chicken means cowardly
fee'd, given a fee, means paid

explanation.surface: A timid worker who was paid very little.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken feed is slang for a trivial sum of cash, as cheap as grain for poultry.

clue.text: A region tranformed in period long ago

indicators.note: the letters of a region are transformed into a new order

explanation.surface: An area changes over a distant era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tranformed' (a misprint for 'transformed') rearranges A REGION.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iron Age is a prehistoric era when iron tools came into use.

clue.text: Impair — with removal of odd bits?

definitions.text: Impair — with removal of odd bits?

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves the second, fourth and sixth of the word

explanation.surface: Damaging something by stripping away its odd pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition and the wordplay: take the even letters of IMPAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil or damage something is to impair it.

clue.text: Take away one bishop inside this vehicle

indicators.note: inside places one and bishop within the subtraction word

parts.note: take away means minus, as in subtraction
I is the Roman numeral for one
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop is driven off in a small vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take away' suggests removing; it is subtraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibus is a small bus carrying a dozen or so passengers.

clue.text: Part in musical providing a good example

parts.note: a musical is a stage show
a piece is a part or portion

explanation.surface: A role in a stage musical that sets a fine example.
explanation.definitionFit: A showpiece is an outstanding specimen displayed as a model of its kind.

clue.text: Like a mountain top seen here? Not very well

definitions.text: Like a mountain top seen here?
definitions.meaning: having peaks, like the jagged outline of a mountain top
British slang for pale and sickly

explanation.definitionFit: Peaky can mean having peaks, and in British usage it also means looking unwell.

clue.text: Preserve a lake as navigable waterway

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it in tins
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Conservationists keep a lake as a channel for boats.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is a man-made channel for boats and barges.

clue.text: Unit of light troops in place in Egypt

parts.note: the lux is the SI unit of illumination
OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Light army units are stationed in Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light troops' reads as lightly armed soldiers; 'light' belongs to the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Luxor is an Egyptian city on the Nile, site of ancient Thebes.

clue.text: A declaration of friendship from Muslim region

parts.note: I'm, short for I am, opens a declaration about oneself
a mate is a friend, so the term of friendship here is mate

explanation.surface: A friendly message sent from a part of the Islamic world.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the friendly phrase as a speaker would declare it, and it runs together into a single word for an imam's domain.
explanation.definitionFit: An imamate is the territory ruled by an imam, an Islamic leader.

clue.text: Wood for steering-wheel not hard to find

indicators.note: not says the hard abbreviation is left out

parts.note: a ship's helm is its wheel or tiller
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Timber for a steering wheel is easy to find.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard to find' reads as easy; 'not' removes H.
explanation.definitionFit: Elm is the timber of the elm tree.

clue.text: Inferior case for collector of coins

parts.note: poor means of low quality, inferior
a box is a case or container

explanation.surface: A shabby case belonging to a numismatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collector of coins' suggests a numismatist; it is a church box for alms.
explanation.definitionFit: A poor box is a church receptacle gathering coins given as charity for the needy.

clue.text: Say in cathedral a lament for the dead

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for say within the cathedral city's name

parts.note: Ely, a small city in Cambridgeshire, is famous for its cathedral
eg (for example) is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A mourning song is recited in a cathedral.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegy is a mournful poem or song, especially one for someone who has died.

clue.text: Preacher has spoken in endless despair

indicators.note: in places the word for spoken within the shortened despair
endless says the final letter of the word for despair is dropped

parts.note: misery is despair or wretchedness
oral means spoken rather than written

explanation.surface: A preacher has spoken while sunk in endless despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last letter of the despair word; a preacher here is anyone who lectures on morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who moralises lectures others on right and wrong, as a sermoniser does.
